quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Who should set the pace in a group of riders?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The rider in back
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider in back
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace for the group. This ensures no riders get left behind.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle:

options.text: The heavier items should go toward the front.
The heavier items should go toward the rear.
Mounting loads behind the rear axle is recommended.
Lighter items should be stored in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heavier items should go toward the front.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items toward the front of the load. Place loads over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that inform drivers of rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When following a car, the best position to ride in is:

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The left or right portions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. This makes you visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: This hand signal means you plan to turn right or change lanes to the right. Bend your left arm at the elbow and point it upward to give this signal.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, it should be:

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the parking space so approaching drivers can more easily see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease your following distance.
Use the vehicle in front of you to help see.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the vehicle in front of you to help see.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: To reduce the amount of time you need to react to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hand near the clutch and brakes. This reduces your reaction time if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Avoid surface hazards.
Prevent access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane position increases your visibility, helps you avoid blind spots and surface hazards, and discourages others from sharing your lane. It should give you an escape route in case a hazard appears.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one at a time, not together. Braking while swerving may cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle requires:

options.text: A lot of traction.
Little traction.
A slow maneuver.
Being done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver. It needs a lot of traction to be done safely. Do not swerve suddenly on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: If the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left portion of a lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
All areas of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. This oil reduces traction when roads are wet. Ride to the side of this center area to stay safe.

questions.question: When making normal stops, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping. Do this for all stops, even normal ones.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam (unless following another car), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and have enough space.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always pick one part of the lane and never leave it.
Change your lane position as conditions warrant.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other vehicles see you more easily.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so other drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as conditions warrant.
questions.explanation: No one lane position is always best. Change your lane position as needed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn your handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: If you must swerve, apply light pressure to the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is better.
You may experience a wind blast on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the driver to return to your lane before they have enough room to do so safely.

questions.question: In which of the following situations should you increase your following distance?

options.text: Traffic is light.
Traffic is heavy.
You can see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
The weather is pleasant and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normally enough. Increase it when conditions need longer stopping distance, such as in bad weather, at night, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually just as powerful as car headlights.
Usually not as powerful as car headlights.
Usually larger than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the rear tire grips the road again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What is the best protection for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Wearing a good leather jacket.
Wearing sturdy boots.
Knowing motorcycle laws well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best protection against crashes is keeping distance from other vehicles. This gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Proper safety gear is also important.

questions.question: How should you choose your lane position?

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Change your position based on different factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on different factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you can be seen best and where you can keep space around you.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: At speeds above 55 mph.
After riding for several hours.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds below 30 mph.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is safest when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane unsafely.
